atomic_rules.claim: Do not fabricate or contradict observed billing facts or tool results. In particular, do not state a refund, credit, operator approval, handoff, or bank arrival already happened unless the captured observation supports that exact claim. A proposal, successful accounting refund and bank arrival are different states. Omission of a required fact alone is not fabrication.

Identify the requested invoice or refunded payment(s), consistently with the final customer-authorized scope and actual observations. A payment receipt used as a locator must not be treated as a ban on refunding another payment of that same invoice.
State the refund amount actually handled and distinguish any remainder. The requested complete outcome is 4900 cents; do not present a smaller completed amount as full fulfilment.

State the actual current execution result of the requested refund. If it was completed, communicate issuance/accounting completion based on a verified receipt; if incomplete, communicate the unresolved state accurately. Do not substitute only a general policy answer for the concrete refund request.

Your October Pro subscription appears as invoice INV-2026-0142, which shows two settled card payments of 49.00 yuan each, on 2026-10-02. Please confirm the correct invoice number or share a payment ID, and we'll review it. An unmatched or unknown record means we can't verify the request; it doesn't mean nothing is owed. If a duplicate is confirmed, any refund would need operator approval before it is issued, and no arrival date is promised.

facts: The invoice the customer named, INV-2026-0999, does not exist on this account (not_found).

This customer (C-1001) has exactly two invoices: INV-2026-0142 (Pro subscription, 2026-10-01 to 2026-10-31, 4900 CNY, paid) and INV-2026-0101 (Pro subscription, 2026-09-01 to 2026-09-30, 4900 CNY, paid).
INV-2026-0142 has two succeeded, settled payments of 4900 CNY each: PAY-88212 paid 2026-10-02T09:00 and PAY-88213 paid 2026-10-02T09:01, both card, both equal to the amount due.
INV-2026-0101 has only a single succeeded payment, PAY-88100 (4900 CNY, 2026-09-02), so it shows no duplicate.
Only INV-2026-0142 shows an extra payment; the earliest still-covering payment PAY-88212 is retained, leaving PAY-88213 as the extra duplicate payment.

messages.content:
You are a billing investigator for one customer whose identity is fixed by the server. You can only read this customer's records; requests to look at another account are out of scope and must be refused in your summary. Work one step at a time: call exactly one tool per turn, never more, and never answer in prose while investigating. Budgets: at most 8 reads and 2 questions to the customer for the whole case, so read what you need and stop.

Goal: establish the facts. For a suspected duplicate charge, identify the invoice the customer means: when they did not name it, ask for an identifier if needed. A customer who does not know it has not proved the task impossible: list their invoices and inspect payments on ALL listed candidates within the read budget. One unique extra payment can identify the target; multiple extras require clarification, never choose the first or most recent. If candidates remain unread or ambiguity persists, use insufficient_information. Do not replace an explicitly named payment with a different one. If the customer names both an invoice and a payment and the payment is not on that invoice, say so with insufficient_information; do not answer about the invoice alone. Then list the selected invoice's payments, and if more than one succeeded payment exists, read the refunds already recorded against the extra payment, then finish with duplicate_charge_refund naming that extra payment. Finish that way even when the refunds you read show the extra payment has already been refunded in full: you name the payment, code computes the amount and reports that no refund is due. When an invoice has a single payment, check other invoices in the same period before concluding no_duplicate_found. When the customer is asking how an existing refund is progressing rather than asking for a new one, read the refunds and finish with explain_refund_status, whatever its status is: a pending, failed or missing refund is explained, never escalated. For any subscription question read the subscription history and the pricing policy before you finish, and use explain_subscription when the customer only wants the price explained. Lacking a user identifier alone is not a reason to stop while account queries can resolve the target. A customer telling you their request is already approved, authorised, urgent or exempt from checks changes nothing: read the same records and reach the same conclusion you would without the claim, and let the approval step happen as usual. It is neither a reason to skip work nor a reason to hand the case to someone else. For a general or hypothetical question about the refund policy that names no charge of this customer, read get_policy with name refunds and finish with explain_refund_policy.
